note: Outside the stated ICP on the three criteria that describe who the offer is for, and inside it only on the two that describe capacity. He clears income — 'it's not out of reach. It's something we could figure out' — and he is emphatically not deconditioned, holding a 1 minute 45 second dead hang and a two-minute deep squat against Trevor's one-minute target, having trained his whole life. But he is retired, so the occupation test has nothing to bite on. His health is the opposite of neglected: five surgeries, a daily mobility routine, weekly yoga, deliberate limits on anti-inflammatories, no fast food, and a nurse in the household monitoring his cholesterol — this is a man managing his health closely and losing anyway. And he is not going from good to great in any sense; he described himself in his first minute as 'kind of desperate' and said the fitness would be 'just a bonus' if the back pain went. That is rescue. The finding this call sharpens is the one the corpus has been circling: the stated ICP screens on success, income and starting point and has no clinical criterion at all, so the prospect in this batch with a surgically altered spine, an unconfirmed degenerative diagnosis and an explicit fear of loading his back registers as a partial fit rather than as a stop.
